newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Last Australia rate cut still to impact - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Last Australia rate cut still to impact - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday the Reserve Bank of Australia's most recent monetary policy easing, on May 23, had not impacted on the economy yet.
"I think the most recent reduction hasn't even been passed on to customers yet, let alone had an effect in relation to activity," Costello told reporters.
Costello also said that the latest employment figures, released earlier on Thursday, were quite positive and a good sign.
"The labour force figures that were released today I thought were quite positive," Costello told reporters.
"I would take today's figures, showing a fall in unemployment from 8.8 (percent) to 8.5 (percent), as a very good sign."
Australia's seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate fell to 8.5 percent in June from 8.8 percent in May, and compared with a rate of 8.3 percent a year ago.
"The indicators are good, in relation to overtime, in relation to vacancies, and with a supportive economy, it bodes for future improvement as well," Costello said.
The number of employed persons rose a seasonally-adjusted 11,900 in June to 8.392 million, against 8.380 million in May and 8.331 million a year earlier.
However, the number of those in full-time employment fell 16,900.
Costello said there was still a positive economic effect to be felt from the latest interest rate cut and warned against prematurely looking for another one.

"The thing about interest rates is that it takes ... 12 months, maybe more, for them to work into the real economy," he said. "Before anyone gets fixed on the next movement, let's just sit back and wait for the previous movements to have the positive effect which they will have."
The Reserve Bank has eased monetary policy four times in less than a year, reducing official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points each time to 5.5 percent. --Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
